own_scenes.desc: A principios de los noventa el metal empieza a perder definición en su periferia: el lite metal se acerca al pop con secciones de cuerda (Damn Yankees), otros grupos meten el funk heredado de las mezclas de punk y funk (Living Colour, Faith No More) cortando el poder del metal con ironía, Jane’s Addiction añade art rock reflexivo y Scatterbrain juega con el género de forma consciente, socavando su autenticidad. Weinstein lo ve como el proceso normal de cambio cultural de un género que conserva su núcleo.

notes.chapter: Cap. 3: Hacer la música: los dioses del metal
notes.text: A finales de los ochenta ya no es raro ver músicos negros e hispanos en el metal: los hispanos se concentran en el speed/thrash y los negros sobre todo en el metal funk de Living Colour y 24-7 Spyz, que aportan su propia cultura musical.

influences.name: Lite metal: pop metal y glam

refs.q: Other groups, influenced by blends of punk and funk are incorporating funk into metal (e.g., Living Color and Faith No More)
refs.para: A new surge of complexity has begun within metal that is making it lose its definition at the periphery. Lite metal deepens its flirtation/romance with pop, as some bands (e.g., Damn Yankees) incorporate string sections, alien to heavy metal’s code, into their music. Other groups, influenced by blends of punk and funk are incorporating funk into metal (e.g., Living Color and Faith No More), often producing a sound the inherent meaning of which cuts metal’s power with irony and takes away much of its force. Others (e.g., Jane’s Addiction) introduce art rock into the mix, creating a reflective music that militates against metal’s directness. Still others (e.g., Scatterbrain) play with the genre self-consciously, undercutting its stance and sensibility of authenticity. All of these developments are too germinal to include in the present discussion, but they indicate that metal is undergoing the normal process of cultural change, even as it retains its core.
refs.chapter: Cap. 2: Heavy metal: la bestia que se niega a morir

refs.q: Hispanics tended to specialize in the speed/thrash subgenre.
refs.para: By the end of the 1980s, however, as metal continued to fragment and absorb other musical elements, black and Hispanic heavy metal musicians were no longer novel. Hispanics tended to specialize in the speed/thrash subgenre. Blacks also could be found in those groups, but they concentrated especially in the funk-oriented metal made by groups such as Living Colour and 24-7 Spyz. That is, they brought the contribution of their separate musical culture to metal, grafting themselves on to it.

podcast.title: Prominence in the 1990s and 2010s Comebacks
podcast.body: Alternative Metal, also known as Alternative Hard Rock, was a prominent genre in the 1990s. In the 2010s, it saw comebacks from older groups like Jane's Addiction, Biohazard, and Faith No More, as well as the emergence of new young bands such as Greta Van Fleet, Turnstile, and The Struts, who were inspired by classic rock. "Alternative Metal, or alternative hard rock, if you prefer, was definitely a thing in the 90s."
